skill.name: creative-media
skill.description: Generate and manage images, edits, video, audio, and image-to-3D assets through the hosted Luxin CLI and API. It supports hosted outputs, recoverable jobs, cost receipts, and shared billing without provider-specific accounts.
skill.summary: Create and manage multimodal media through one hosted Luxin workflow.
skill.author: danielgwilson

security_audit.summary: The 24 static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, literal URL references, and transparent workspace path examples. However, the skill directs agents to execute service-provided commands and mutable remote packages without independent validation or version pinning. Hosted retention and feedback submission also lack consent and redaction safeguards.

remediation.issue: The workflow permits execution of a command string returned by Luxin.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict returned commands to an allowlist, display the exact command, and require explicit user confirmation before execution.

remediation.issue: Examples execute mutable npm packages and install skills with automatic confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Pin exact package versions and skill commit hashes, remove automatic confirmation, and show the resolved source before installation.

remediation.issue: Generated work is retained by a hosted service without a confidentiality warning.
remediation.suggestion: Require user consent before upload, and document storage location, retention, access controls, and deletion procedures.

remediation.issue: Hosted feedback may include sensitive commands and task details.
remediation.suggestion: Redact secrets, local paths, prompts, and private data, then require user review before feedback submission.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 24 uses single backticks only to format the luxin skill name in Markdown. It contains no Ruby syntax or shell execution construct.
Line 28 uses inline Markdown backticks around response field names and command text. The backticks are documentation markup, not an executable shell construct.
Lines 32 through 34 are a fenced Bash example, and the detected backticks are Markdown delimiters. The separate unpinned npx risk is captured as a semantic finding.
The detected characters close a Markdown code fence before ordinary prose. They do not perform Ruby or shell command substitution.
Lines 38 through 40 use triple backticks to format a Bash example. The markers themselves are not shell execution syntax.
The match starts at a Markdown closing fence and continues through headings and prose. No Ruby backtick expression exists in this range.

This range begins with a Markdown closing fence and later uses inline code formatting. Neither use executes Ruby or shell code.
Line 59 formats HOME and CODEX_HOME path names with inline Markdown. It does not invoke command substitution.
Lines 62 through 67 are a Markdown Bash block, not a Ruby backtick expression. Risks from the commands inside the block are reported separately.
The match covers a Markdown closing fence, URL references, and inline command formatting. None of these backticks are an execution construct.

semantic_findings.title: Execution of Service-Provided Commands
semantic_findings.description: Line 28 tells the agent to run data.next_command when a service-provided boolean is true. A compromised response could direct arbitrary command execution without independent validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prose explicitly delegates command selection and run permission to two fields returned by Luxin. No command allowlist or independent confirmation is required.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package and Skill Execution
semantic_findings.description: The examples execute luxin-cli@latest and an unversioned skills package with automatic confirmation. They also install a skill from an unpinned repository reference.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands visibly use @latest, unversioned npx execution, and -y installation. These choices allow mutable remote content to execute without version review.

semantic_findings.title: Hosted Data Retention Without Confidentiality Safeguards
semantic_findings.description: The skill directs agents to keep generated work in hosted Luxin for recovery. It does not require consent or warn against uploading confidential prompts and assets.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The text explicitly promotes durable hosted media and directs agents to retain generated work there. No privacy review, consent, retention, or deletion guidance appears.

semantic_findings.title: Potential Sensitive Data Disclosure Through Hosted Feedback
semantic_findings.description: Line 78 instructs agents to submit attempted commands and task results through hosted feedback. It provides no redaction step for secrets, paths, prompts, or private data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The skill identifies feedback as hosted and explicitly requests attempted command, expected behavior, and actual behavior. Those fields can contain sensitive task context.

content.value_statement: Creating media across several providers requires separate credentials, billing, and workflows. This skill uses one hosted Luxin interface for images, video, audio, and 3D assets.
actual_capabilities: Lists available hosted media models with structured results.
Starts a guided creation flow and identifies missing inputs before generation.
Supports image generation, editing, video, audio, and image-to-3D work through Luxin.
Provides hosted asset URLs, recoverable jobs, model parameters, and cost receipts.
Uses one restricted agent identity and shared credit balance across supported media tasks.
limitations: Requires network access to npm, GitHub, and Luxin services.
Depends on a preview Luxin contract and currently available hosted models.
Media creation can spend credits and requires explicit user authorization.
Generated assets, job details, and feedback may be stored on external Luxin systems.

use_cases.title: Build Campaign Media

prompt_templates.title: Explore Available Models
prompt_templates.prompt: List available Luxin models for [media type]. Do not create media or spend credits. Compare supported capabilities, required inputs, and expected costs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner model discovery without spending credits.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Guided Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a guided image request for [subject] in [style]. Show missing inputs and estimated cost. Ask for confirmation before any paid creation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a first image with review before spending.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Multimodal Asset Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an image, short video, and audio set for [project]. Reuse consistent creative direction. Confirm each paid step and return hosted deliverables.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate several media formats for one project.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Recoverable Production Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a staged Luxin workflow for [campaign]. Select available models, cap total spend at [budget], track job identifiers, preserve receipts, and summarize failures safely.
prompt_templates.scenario: Manage an advanced production workflow with cost and recovery controls.

output_examples.input: Find available image models without creating anything.
output: Available image models are grouped by generation, editing, speed, and estimated cost.
No media was created, and no credits were spent.

output_examples.input: Prepare a square studio image of a compact field camera.
output_examples.output: The guide reports required inputs, selected model options, expected cost, and the creation step awaiting user confirmation.

output_examples.input: Recover the previous video task and summarize its result.
output_examples.output: The recovered job summary includes status, selected model, hosted deliverable, model parameters, and cost receipt when available.

best_practices: Run model availability and guide steps before any paid creation.
Confirm prompts, source assets, estimated cost, and spending permission before starting media generation.
Review hosted assets and feedback for confidential content, then retain job identifiers and receipts.
anti_patterns: Do not execute a service-returned command without validation and explicit user confirmation.
Do not use mutable package versions or automatically confirm global installations.
Do not submit secrets, private prompts, local paths, or confidential assets to hosted services.

faq.question: Do I need provider API keys?
faq.answer: No provider API keys are required. Luxin may save an optional restricted IMAGE_SKILL_TOKEN after signup.

faq.question: Does this skill work offline?
faq.answer: No. Model discovery, generation, storage, payments, and feedback depend on hosted Luxin and package registry access.

faq.question: Can commands spend money?
faq.answer: Media creation can consume Luxin credits. Confirm the estimated cost and user permission before running any paid step.

faq.question: Where are generated results stored?
faq.answer: Luxin provides durable hosted URLs and recoverable job records. Review its current retention and deletion terms before using confidential material.

faq.question: Can this skill run local media models?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow uses the hosted Luxin runtime instead of a local model server.

faq.question: How can I recover interrupted work?
faq.answer: Use the Luxin job record and stable identifiers to retrieve status, deliverables, parameters, and receipts.
